# Make state-version discovery and recovery examples safe to copy

## Current scope

This body applies the already selected post-PR212 F01–F10/A01–A05 amendment after its merge/service-acceptance and independent amendment-review boundary. It does not assert that implementation or acceptance has occurred.

Repository: TerraformStyleGuide; native issue: #23. Own seven published Bash surfaces: `SR-AWS-DISCOVERY`, `SR-AWS-RECOVERY`, `SR-AZURE-DISCOVERY`, `SR-AZURE-RECOVERY`, `SR-GCS-DISCOVERY`, `SR-GCS-RECOVERY`, and `SR-HCP-DISCOVERY`. Preserve their identification so the harness executes the actual final published snippets. Separate discovery from deliberate exact-version retrieval. Never auto-select latest or mutate remote state. Check current primary provider documentation at implementation for identifier restrictions, supported bucket/account classes, permissions, version retention and retrieval behavior; document a limited supported subset rather than inventing incompatible restrictions.

Write sensitive outputs only to fresh protected destinations outside Git and inappropriate shared storage. Do not overwrite existing files or links. Do not log tokens, signed URLs or state. A typed no-competing-writer phrase is a stated precondition, not proof. Inspect what can actually be verified; bound race/ownership claims honestly. Use provider-native no-clobber support where available and safe publication/cleanup ownership. Before publication, a failure leaves no final file and cleans only proven owned temporary data. After publication or ownership uncertainty, retain the sensitive output privately and fail; never delete a successfully recovered file merely to satisfy an absence assertion. Preserve the primary error or signal; report cleanup-only failure distinctly.

Use network-free provider stubs to execute the exact seven snippets and test deliberate identifier/version preservation, wrong version, unsupported input, existing file/link, partial failure, secret suppression and safe cleanup at each phase. Test documented runtime requirements on supported environments; do not assume wrapper tests prove copied snippets. Keep adjacent manual backups, destructive state commands, corruption recovery and older overlapping examples inventoried in the separate destructive-recovery follow-up. Generate derived guide outputs from sources and run applicable native content, lint, metadata and CI checks. Complete through the shared lifecycle; a PS counterpart change requires a demonstrated common need, not a mandatory cycle.

## Provider behavior retained

| Provider | Required behavior |
| --- | --- |
| AWS S3 | Discover versions for the exact key; retrieve only the deliberately supplied version. Explain Enabled/Suspended/null behavior, expiration/permanent deletion, general-purpose bucket scope, ListBucketVersions/GetObjectVersion permissions and applicable KMS decryption. Recheck current primary bucket-class and KMS documentation before implementation; do not change bucket versioning. |
| Azure Blob | Discover the exact blob's versions and retrieve the chosen version with no-overwrite support. Explain authentication/read permissions, versioning prerequisites and documented unsupported account classes. |
| GCS | Distinguish retained Object Versioning generations from soft-delete recovery; discover the exact object and retrieve the explicitly selected generation. Explain list/get permissions and supported no-clobber behavior; add no soft-delete restoration. |
| HCP Terraform | Discover the selected workspace's state-version API data into a fresh protected response file with bounded paging and explicit host/workspace/page inputs. Protect bearer tokens, signed URLs and returned state metadata. Do not download or apply a state automatically. |

Document the supported identifier subset against current provider rules, preserve accepted location/version bytes, reject missing/unsafe inputs before provider or filesystem work, and prove those properties with the actual published snippets. Retain the scoped seven IDs, not a permanent source-hash or arbitrary grammar protocol.

## Delivery and evidence

For implementation changes, use the plan's shared lifecycle: implementation and relevant behavior/security validation, authenticated independent review, separate fresh independent final-quality audit, normal head-matched merge, actual landed readback and changed-service acceptance. Preserve the full validate/options/unique weighted rubric/scores/selection process for each distinct confirmed finding. Reuse standing in-scope authority and authorized actual Claude substitution; failed Codex remains failed, pending requests and attempt caps remain binding. Candidate flags/tests do not grant maintenance authority. Required native checks must truthfully state what they prove. No settings, administrator override, force, credentials or bypass authority is created here.

The prior writer, release-prose, duplicated review and compulsory reverse-cycle requirements replaced below are superseded, not implemented. Historical issue discussions and implementation evidence remain history. Complete only the retained outcome and its real acceptance gates; do not manufacture a PR for a proved no-change applicability result.
